questions.q: What is a Subledger Accounting Method?
options: A report that lists every journal entry in a period
The top-level object assigned to a ledger that points, per subledger application, to the rule sets to use for its events
A single account rule that derives one segment value
A type of subledger application like Payables or Receivables
questions.explain: The accounting method is a container assigned to a ledger; it does not hold logic directly but points to the journal entry rule sets for each subledger application.

questions.q: Which rule type decides whether a given journal line is a debit or a credit, and whether it should even appear?
options: Description rules
Supporting references
Journal line rules
Account rules
questions.explain: Journal line rules determine which lines appear on the entry and whether each is a debit or a credit.

questions.q: What is the role of account rules within a journal entry rule set?
options: They determine which General Ledger account, or account segment, each journal line should post to
They schedule when Create Accounting runs
They validate a supplier's bank account number
They build the human-readable description of a line
questions.explain: Account rules derive the GL account or segment values for a journal line; description rules, by contrast, build the line's text description.

questions.q: How do the four rule types (journal line rules, account rules, description rules, supporting references) relate to an event class?
options: They are unrelated to event classes entirely
They are bundled into a subledger journal entry rule set, which is assigned to an event class (and optionally a more specific event type)
Each rule type requires its own separate accounting method
Only account rules can ever be assigned to an event class
questions.explain: A journal entry rule set bundles all four rule types and is assigned to a specific event class, optionally refined by event type.

questions.q: Why might a company assign two different accounting methods across its ledgers?
options: Oracle requires every company to use at least two methods
To report the same underlying transactions under two different accounting standards, such as local GAAP and IFRS, via a primary and a secondary ledger
Because journal line rules can only be used once
There is never a valid reason to use more than one method
questions.explain: A primary ledger and a secondary ledger can each use a different accounting method so the same events are accounted differently for different reporting standards.
